findings.original: When they change us for others? Is it sport?
findings.current: when they swap us for other women? Is it for fun?
findings.issue: "Sport" here means sexual play; "for fun" flattens the sexual sense Emilia is pointing at (same issue recurs in line 16, "an appetite for fun").
findings.proposed: when they swap us for other women? Is it for the pleasure of sex?

findings.original: Desires for sport, and frailty, as men have?
findings.current: an appetite for fun, and weakness, just as men do?
findings.issue: "Desires for sport" is sexual appetite; "appetite for fun" reads as innocent amusement.
findings.proposed: an appetite for sexual pleasure, and weakness, just as men do?

findings.original: If wives do fall: say that they slack their duties,
findings.current: when wives fall: say they neglect their duties in bed
findings.issue: The marital-duty (sexual) reading is standard, but "in bed" makes explicit what the original leaves as "duties"; acceptable gloss, flagged for the editor.
findings.proposed: when wives fall: say they neglect their marital duties

findings.original: It is the cause, it is the cause, my soul,
findings.current: That's the reason, that's the reason, my soul —
findings.issue: "Cause" carries the legal sense (the case, the charge being judged) as well as the reason; "reason" alone loses Othello's self-image as a judge carrying out justice.
findings.proposed: It's the cause — the crime on trial — it's the cause, my soul;

findings.original: As I have to be hurt. O gull! O dolt!
findings.current: that I have to bear the hurt. Oh, you sucker! You idiot!
findings.issue: "Sucker" is modern American slang; "gull" means dupe, which can be said plainly without the slang.
findings.proposed: that I have to bear the hurt. Oh, you dupe! You idiot!

findings.original: But why should honour outlive honesty?
findings.current: But why should a good name outlive honor itself?
findings.issue: Using "honor" to translate "honesty" (integrity, virtue) is confusing, since "honour" is the word being glossed; the contrast is reputation vs. real integrity.
findings.proposed: But why should my reputation outlive my integrity?

findings.original: Perplex’d in the extreme; of one whose hand,
findings.current: was driven utterly out of his mind; of one whose hand,
findings.issue: "Perplexed" means utterly confused or distraught, not insane; "out of his mind" slightly overstates it in a speech where the wording matters.
findings.proposed: was thrown into utter turmoil; of one whose hand,
